Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 21
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: Latin American
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Animator
  trauma_type: Witnessed domestic violence (childhood)
  pcl5: 39

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Object Throwing: Throwing objects, Visual (Photos): Related photos, Auditory (Sounds): Related sounds
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Future Plans: Making any plans for the future, Restrict Eating: control eating strictly to feel in control, Avoid Perpetrator Cues: Anything that reminds me of the person who harmed me
  Threat: Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively, Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
  Memory: More Real Than Normal: My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things, Olfactory Recall: When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened., Blocked Before Complete: I find myself pushing the memory away before I can fully recall it
  Negative Appraisals: Low Coping: I can't deal with even the slightest upset, No Accountability: The people responsible have faced no consequences, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me

Vignette:
Ana had grown up in a household where the sounds of shattering glass and screams were all too familiar. As a child, she would often cower in her room, covering her ears with her hands, praying that the argument between her parents wouldn't escalate further. One particular incident still lingered vividly in her mind - the night her father threw a vase at her mother, shattering it into a hundred pieces on the kitchen floor. The smell of freshly brewed coffee and the sound of crunching glass underfoot had become indelibly linked to that moment. As Ana entered adulthood, she began to notice how certain triggers would transport her back to those tumultuous nights. Throwing objects, even something as mundane as a friend tossing a frisbee in the park, made her flinch. Photos of happy families or couples only served as painful reminders of what she had witnessed growing up. Even sounds - the crash of a pot, the raised voice of an argumentative stranger on the street - sent her heart racing. Ana's coping mechanisms were born out of this anxiety. She began to avoid making plans for the future, terrified that some unforeseen event would shatter the fragile sense of security she had constructed around herself. Her strict control over food intake was another attempt at exerting control in a chaotic world. "If I can just keep my eating habits in check," she'd tell herself, "I'll be okay." Anything that reminded her of her father - his cologne, his favorite foods - made her stomach turn. Ana's emotions often got the better of her. Irritability and anger outbursts became more frequent as she struggled to contain the pent-up emotions from her childhood. Her friends began to notice a change in her demeanor, commenting on how "on edge" she seemed all the time. Ana couldn't explain why; even small movements nearby - a sudden tap on the shoulder or an unexpected knock at the door - made her jump. Her memories of that fateful night remained more real and vivid than any other recollection from her childhood. Sometimes, when she closed her eyes, the smell of freshly brewed coffee wafted back, transporting her to that moment in time. Yet, whenever she tried to recall the full sequence of events, something inside her would shut down, blocking out the details before they could fully surface. Ana often felt helpless in the face of life's uncertainties. She was convinced that even minor setbacks were catastrophic events waiting to unfold. No one had ever held her father accountable for his actions; why should she trust that anyone else would be brought to justice? Her self-perceived inability to cope with adversity only added fuel to this fire, leaving Ana feeling perpetually trapped in a never-ending cycle of fear and hypervigilance. As an animator, Ana found solace in the creative process. However, even her art began to suffer as her anxiety took hold. Projects stalled, deadlines were missed, and she started questioning whether she was cut out for this career path after all. The pressure mounted until Ana finally broke down, recognizing that something had to give. With a deep breath, she picked up the phone and made an appointment with a therapist, hoping against hope that someone could help her unravel the tangled threads of her past and show her a way forward - one where memories didn't haunt her every waking moment, and triggers didn't dictate her life's narrative.
